newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia lashes out at violent opposition groups.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia lashes out at violent opposition groups.

text.p: Ethiopia's leader on Tuesday vowed to smash legal opposition organisations he accused of giving sanctuary to "terrorist" groups.

"Nothing will stop the Government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia from smashing organisations which provide safe haven to terrorist individuals or organisations," Prime Minister Meles Zenawi said.
His statement was issued on the eve of the sixth anniversary of the arrival of rebel forces in the capital Addis Ababa in 1991 to topple Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam.
Meles said his government was committed to cooperating with opposition groups that pursued their causes by peaceful means.
He gave no names but said his government knew of legally established organisations in Ethiopia pretending to be peaceful but "providing safe haven to elements of organised terrorism".
He said action had not been taken against them because the authorities had believed that they would come to their senses.
"Such organisations have to clearly define their roles: either adhere to peaceful means of struggle or side with anti-peace and anti-democratic elements," Meles said.
Meles condemned attackers who tossed grenades in hotels, a bar and a supermarket last month as "terrorists which have declared war on the country's popular democratic constitution".
One person was killed and 86 people including foreigners were wounded. No group has claimed responsibility for them.
The government last year blamed Moslem fundamentalists for a series of bombings and sent its troops, backed by helicopter gunships, into western Somalia to strike Moslem fundamentalist bases.
Ethiopian police said earlier this month they shot dead in Addis Ababa a man they had identified as a leader of an underground group who had resisted arrest and tried to flee.

But an independent Ethiopian human rights group said the dead man, Assefa Maru, was a member of its executive and the executive committee of the Ethiopian Teachers Association and was innocent. It said Assefa was unarmed when he was killed.
The Ethiopian Human Rights Council demanded an official investigation into the shooting.
